open_points.subject: FlowActivation creation (M18) / activate flow action
open_points.text: K-08: "A read-only flow is activated by the kernel once proven"; Primary actions: "activate a flow | agent or owner asks; the kernel activates a proven read-only version at once"; M18 source: "The kernel, after proof and, for effectful versions, the owner."
open_points.question: For a proven read-only flow version, is a FlowActivation created automatically at proof time, or only when someone calls the activate action?
options: Automatic on successful proof (compose-and-prove can create activation).
Only the activate action can create activation; read-only just skips owner approval.
Both paths are allowed (auto on proof and also explicit activate idempotently returns/creates).
open_points.default_guess: Only the activate action creates FlowActivation; for read-only it succeeds immediately without owner approval.

open_points.subject: Effect authority for draft-write resend after not_applied/unknown (K-08 vs M26)
open_points.text: State 0 product statement: "... asks the owner before each effect of the classes K-08 stops for — a `draft-write` runs under the owner's activation of the flow instead"; K-08 stop classes are `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`; M26 lifecycle: "Sending again after `not_applied` is a new attempt under a fresh approval, never under a standing approval (K-08)." and M26 authority: "... for a `draft-write` send the flow activation ... except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records the fresh approval it needed."
open_points.question: Does a draft-write operation ever require an EffectApproval, specifically when resending after `not_applied`/resolved unknown?
options: No; draft-write always runs under flow activation only, including resends.
Yes; draft-write normally uses activation, but resend after `not_applied`/resolved unknown requires a fresh approval.
Yes; any resend of any non-read class requires fresh approval.
open_points.default_guess: No; draft-write never requires per-effect approval and always uses flow activation as authority.

open_points.subject: FlowActivation actor attribution for read-only activation (M18/M27/K-15)
open_points.text: K-15: "Records name the kernel as the actor of what it does on its own ... activation of a proven read-only flow"; Primary action: "activate a flow | agent or owner asks; the kernel activates a proven read-only version at once"; M18 carries only `activated_by`.
open_points.question: When a user invokes activate for a read-only proven version, should `activated_by` be `kernel` (automatic step) or the requesting principal?
options: `activated_by` is the requester because activation happened in their action call.
Record both initiator and decider/actor (requires additional field/model fact).
